decisions.source_term_or_construction: set; naive set theory
decisions.intended_sense: No qualifying Javanese set-theory witness was found. Kumpulan has only ordinary gathering senses in the checked dictionary and is retained as negative evidence. The official borrowing rule, government-edited Javanese mathematics use of international terms, and direct scholarly use of teori support the borrowing pattern, while each mathematical sense is defined from OpenLogic rather than Indonesian. The complete term remains provisional and reversible.

The complete term remains provisional and reversible.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: extensionality
decisions.intended_sense: The international technical stem remains a controlled borrowing. OLP-0005 defines the exact biconditional, and OLP-0013 uses extensionality only to show that two unequal candidate sets cannot both be identical to one order relation; no canon passage is claimed to attest the set-theoretic sense.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: enumeration; enumerable; enumerability; countability
decisions.intended_sense: The canon directly supports general number/count vocabulary and scholarly prose, not countable infinity or enumeration theory. OLP-0027 preserves the elementary list-or-surjection-from-positive-integers approach and the attributed bijection-with-Nat-or-an-initial-segment alternative. OLP-0029 controls the family by an informal list with every member at a finite position, a formal surjection from positive integers for nonempty sets, a separate empty-set case, the equivalent natural-number and finite-initial-segment formulations, and an explicit equation between the tokenized enumerable label and bisa didhaptar. OLP-0031 keeps enumerable unions distinct from finite unions and explicitly states the needed choice assumption for an arbitrary indexed family. OLP-0038 gives the set-theoretic alternative directly: an enumeration is a bijection whose domain is either all natural numbers or a finite initial segment, while the empty set is handled separately; the equivalent natural-number surjection and injection characterizations remain explicit. OLP-0039 proves non-enumerability by showing that every proposed Nat-indexed list omits a constructed element, for both infinite binary sequences and the powerset of Nat. OLP-0040 transfers a hypothetical powerset enumeration through a surjective characteristic-sequence map and thereby reduces enumeration of Bin^omega to enumeration of Pow(Nat). Avoidable active and passive verb forms built on enumerasi are replaced by direct Javanese listing language or menehi/diwenehi enumerasi tumrap. No computability requirement is introduced. The family remains high-uncertainty and reversible rather than conventionally attested.
decisions.chosen_rendering: enumerasi; bisa didhaptar; enumerabilitas; bisa dietung (countable sense, source-defined)
decisions.rationale: The canon directly supports general number/count vocabulary and scholarly prose, not countable infinity or enumeration theory. OLP-0027 preserves the elementary list-or-surjection-from-positive-integers approach and the attributed bijection-with-Nat-or-an-initial-segment alternative. OLP-0029 controls the family by an informal list with every member at a finite position, a formal surjection from positive integers for nonempty sets, a separate empty-set case, the equivalent natural-number and finite-initial-segment formulations, and an explicit equation between the tokenized enumerable label and bisa didhaptar. OLP-0031 keeps enumerable unions distinct from finite unions and explicitly states the needed choice assumption for an arbitrary indexed family. OLP-0038 gives the set-theoretic alternative directly: an enumeration is a bijection whose domain is either all natural numbers or a finite initial segment, while the empty set is handled separately; the equivalent natural-number surjection and injection characterizations remain explicit. OLP-0039 proves non-enumerability by showing that every proposed Nat-indexed list omits a constructed element, for both infinite binary sequences and the powerset of Nat. OLP-0040 transfers a hypothetical powerset enumeration through a surjective characteristic-sequence map and thereby reduces enumeration of Bin^omega to enumeration of Pow(Nat). Avoidable active and passive verb forms built on enumerasi are replaced by direct Javanese listing language or menehi/diwenehi enumerasi tumrap. No computability requirement is introduced. The family remains high-uncertainty and reversible rather than conventionally attested.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: pairing function; encode; code; decode
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0031 defines a pairing function broadly as an injection from A times B into Nat and defines a code as its value on a pair. Its final exercise now enumerates the range before applying the inverse and separately handles an empty product. OLP-0032 gives the bijective code h(n,m)=2^n(2m+1)-1 and separately the injective positive code j(n,m)=2^n3^m, explicitly noting that a nonsurjective encoding has only a partial inverse. These constructions control the coding direction; no native Javanese coding-theory attestation is claimed.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: array; row; column; triangular number; numerical power
decisions.intended_sense: In OLP-0030, larikan rong dimensi remains an explicit high-uncertainty descriptive form fixed by the displayed grids, row and column coordinates and axis labels; no native array-theory attestation is claimed. OLP-0031 corrects the frozen strict triangular-number bound to an inclusive bound, matching the sequence 0, 1, 3, 6 and k(k+1)/2, while retaining wilangan segitiga as source-defined terminology. Gunggung supports numerical sum and rambang directly supports numerical powers; rambang is not transferred to powersets. English ordinal th in OLP-0031 is rendered by preceding kaping, with an empty text-only TeX exponent to preserve structure without residual English.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: truth table; truth function

The formulas control every specialist sense; no native Javanese logic-textbook attestation is claimed.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: non-enumerable; diagonal method; diagonalization
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0033 defines non-enumerability through the absence of a surjection from the positive integers and then proves it with two list-dependent diagonal constructions. JV-D015 now qualifies the surjection characterization to nonempty enumerable sets and explains beside the claim that the empty set is enumerable although no function from the positive integers to it exists. OLP-0039 repeats the two arguments under the Nat-bijection convention. In both units the constructed sequence or subset differs from every indexed proposal. Ora bisa didhaptar remains a descriptive rendering and the diagonal terms remain provisional borrowings; no native Javanese set-theory attestation is claimed.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: reduction; reduce
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0034 fixes the reduction direction operationally: an enumeration of A is transformed into one of B by a surjection A to B, so enumerating B reduces to enumerating A. OLP-0040 restates that direction under the alternate enumeration convention and instantiates it with the surjection sending each subset of Nat to its characteristic binary sequence. A hypothetical enumeration of Pow(Nat) would then enumerate all Bin^omega, contradicting the preceding theorem. Exercises preserve every source and target space. Avoidable ngenumerasi forms are replaced by menehi enumerasi tumrap or direct enumerasi tumrap constructions, while reduksi and ngreduksi remain adapted provisional borrowings under the orthographic policy. No effective or computable reduction condition is implied and no native Javanese computability-theory attestation is claimed.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: arithmetization
decisions.intended_sense: Aritmetisasi adapts the international technical stem under the checked borrowing policy. OLP-0041 fixes its chapter-local sense as the construction of multiple number systems within naive set theory, with ordered imports for integers, rationals, reals, cuts, reflections, detail checking and Cauchy sequences. It does not mean assigning Goedel numbers to syntax here. The canon supports academic prose, borrowing and general number vocabulary, but no native Javanese foundations text directly attests this specialist term.

OLP-0044 fixes the formal sense as a real number outside the rationals, then proves that square root of two has that status by geometric descent and the even-numerator/even-denominator contradiction. No specialized native Javanese attestation is claimed.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: Completeness Property; upper bound; lower bound; least upper bound; greatest lower bound
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0044 defines completeness compositionally and exactly: every nonempty set of reals that has an upper bound has a least upper bound. Its rational counterexample has upper bounds but no least rational upper bound. OLP-0045 uses the dual greatest-lower-bound phrase while motivating cuts. Capitalization marks the named property. The canon supports number vocabulary and academic definition prose, while ordinary jangkep does not itself attest this technical property.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: cut; cuts (Dedekind construction)
decisions.intended_sense: The official dictionary directly records potongan with an ordinary cut or slice sense. OLP-0045 alone controls the formal Dedekind sense by three exact conditions: a nonempty proper initial segment of the rationals with no greatest member. Inclusion orders the cuts, and the union proof verifies all three conditions before proving leastness. The Indonesian dictionary definition is lexical scope evidence rather than a semantic pivot, and no native Javanese real-analysis attestation is claimed.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: commutative ring; ordered ring
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0047 fixes the two structures by formula: the commutative ring has eight displayed laws, and the ordered ring adds a total order compatible with addition and multiplication by nonnegative elements. Ring is retained as an internationally recognizable algebraic borrowing and katata follows the established ordering vocabulary. The canon supports formal-logic and scholarly definitional register plus general relation language, but it does not attest these algebraic compounds as conventional Javanese.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: Cauchy sequence; tends to zero; limit
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0048 defines a Cauchy sequence as a function from Nat to Rat whose values become pairwise epsilon-close beyond some natural bound, and defines tending to zero by the corresponding absolute-value condition. Equivalence is then fixed by the difference tending to zero. Rerangken is the established sequence word, nyedhaki gives the convergence description, and limit is a controlled international borrowing. The canon supports orthography, general function and number language and scholarly register, but no specialized native analysis attestation is claimed.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: closure; closed under the successor function
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0051 defines X as f-closed exactly when every f(x) for x in X remains in X, and defines the closure of o as the intersection of all such sets containing o. The lemma proves containment of o, closure and leastness; JV-D063 makes explicit its self-map scope. OLP-0054 generalizes from one generator to a subset and uses that closure in the Schröder-Bernstein sandwich proof; JV-D064 states the corresponding self-map and carrier-subset scope needed by the generalized definition and lemma. Tutupan and katutup transparently distinguish the generated object from the preservation property; the canon supports general function, member and scholarly-definition language but does not attest this specialist closure terminology.
decisions.chosen_rendering: tutupan; katutup marang fungsi panerus

decisions.source_term_or_construction: Dedekind algebra; successor function; arithmetical induction
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0051 fixes a Dedekind algebra by the three exact conditions o outside the range of f, injectivity of f, and A equal to the f-closure of o. Its successor discussion fixes zero, injectivity and repeated generation. OLP-0052 supplies the induction theorem. Aljabar and aritmetis are controlled adaptations, fungsi has general canon support, and panerus is compositionally transparent; no native Javanese foundations source directly attests the complete compounds.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: recursive definition; exponentiation; isomorphic; structuralist
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0052 fixes the recursive clauses for addition, multiplication and exponentiation over an arbitrary Dedekind algebra; OLP-0053 compares such algebras through isomorphism and reports the structuralist use of that result. The international stems are recognizable adapted scholarly borrowings. The canon supports their orthography, academic prose frame, number and arithmetic components only; the exact formulas and arguments control the specialist meanings, and no native Javanese foundations attestation is claimed.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: propositional logic; propositional variable; propositional or logical connective
decisions.intended_sense: Logika is directly attested in scholarly Javanese and the official orthographic table supports logika and logis. Proposisional, variabel proposisional and konektif remain provisional adapted technical expressions. OLP-0057 states their roles and preserves all five connective symbols; OLP-0058 supplies the exact formation clauses. OLP-0071 applies Aturan Proposisional to the complete LK propositional-rule section while the displayed formulas and left/right rule labels fix the specialist scope, so no canon passage is treated as formal-logic authority. OLP-0100 applies Aturan Proposisional to the complete tableau connective-rule section while the displays fix every polarity. OLP-0107 revalidates konektif proposisional as the class containing the conjunction, disjunction and conditional operators treated by nine tableaux.
decisions.chosen_rendering: logika proposisional; variabel proposisional; konektif proposisional utawa logis
decisions.rationale: Logika is directly attested in scholarly Javanese and the official orthographic table supports logika and logis. OLP-0100 applies Aturan Proposisional to the complete tableau connective-rule section while the displays fix every polarity. OLP-0107 revalidates konektif proposisional as the class containing the conjunction, disjunction and conditional operators treated by nine tableaux.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: negation; conjunction; disjunction; material conditional; biconditional
decisions.intended_sense: Logika is directly attested and the canon supports controlled borrowing and academic exposition, but none of the five complete connective names is attested as a mathematical-logic term. OLP-0058 preserves each symbol, formation clause and primitive-basis abbreviation exactly; OLP-0061 supplies the truth clauses. OLP-0071 uses the connective symbols themselves in the four rule headings and preserves every negation, conjunction, disjunction and conditional left/right rule, so those formal roles do not depend on unattested lexical inference. The English and Latin aliases bottom, top, falsum and verum are retained only as explicitly attributed source-language names with Javanese glosses, not claimed as conventional Javanese terminology. OLP-0100 preserves both signed tableau rules for negation, conjunction, disjunction and the material conditional, including every branch shape. OLP-0101 preserves the material conditional in the final invalid existential-to-universal countertableau. OLP-0102 grows the worked tableau by True conjunction and then True negation, preserving both signs and the exact closure step. OLP-0103 preserves every connective in three worked tableau constructions and 24 propositional exercise items. OLP-0104 preserves negation, conjunction and the material conditional through all three quantified worked tableaux and nine exercises. OLP-0107 preserves panyelakan, panggandhengan, pamisahan and implikasi through their exact signed expansion rules and derivability claims. OLP-0114 preserves all 14 propositional axiom schemas for conjunction, disjunction, conditional, negation, truth and falsity with their exact labels.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: satisfaction; satisfiable; unsatisfiable
decisions.intended_sense: Nyukupi has only an ordinary fulfill-or-meet reading in the checked language evidence; no model-theoretic attestation is claimed. OLP-0057 states the technical relation with the valuation as subject and the formula as object. OLP-0061 labels it transparently as relasi nyukupi, defines every recursive clause, and proves equivalence with evaluation value True; panyukupan remains only a provisional descriptive noun in earlier overview prose. The specialization is source-defined, explicit and reversible. OLP-0091 places panyukupan on the semantic side of its opening contrast, opposed explicitly to syntactic derivability and nonderivability. OLP-0095 quantifies over structures or valuations satisfying every open assumption and preserves every positive and negative satisfaction polarity. OLP-0097 preserves satisfaction of the combined assumption sets, both premise formulas and the identity-elimination conclusion. OLP-0105 places panyukupan on the semantic side of its opening contrast, opposed explicitly to definitions through the existence of closed tableaux. OLP-0109 defines satisfaction for both signs, sets, branches and whole tableaux, preserving every positive and negative semantic polarity. OLP-0111 proves that reflexive identity and both signed identity replacements preserve satisfaction of a tableau branch.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: tautology; semantic entailment or consequence; contingent
decisions.intended_sense: The canon supports scholarly logika and semantik, general truth vocabulary, academic prose and controlled borrowing; it does not attest these complete formal notions. OLP-0057 distinguishes their quantifier patterns. OLP-0062 defines tautology, entailment, satisfiability and contingency through exact valuation quantifiers and the satisfaction relation; its explanatory gloss says that from Gamma, A is an akibat semantis, avoiding the causal verb ngakibatake. The adapted labels and descriptive consequence phrase remain provisional and source-controlled. OLP-0091 retains akibat for entailment in the list of semantic notions, while the following clauses distinguish it from the provability relation. OLP-0095 proves semantic entailment from natural-deduction derivability and keeps that relation distinct in every induction case. OLP-0105 retains akibat for entailment in the list of semantic notions, while the following definitions distinguish it from tableau provability. OLP-0109 derives semantic entailment from tableau provability and keeps the finite signed premise witness distinct from the final model condition.

decisions.intended_sense: Use transparent descriptive phrases in academic prose. The complete formation and parsing vocabulary remains provisional rather than canon-attested.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: uniform substitution; local determination; semantic deduction theorem
decisions.intended_sense: Retain controlled adapted technical compounds under the borrowing policy. OLP-0059 defines substitusi seragam with every occurrence, replacement site and simultaneous variable-to-formula pairing explicit. OLP-0061 defines local determination by agreement on exactly the variables occurring in A and concludes equality of the two evaluations of A. OLP-0062 fixes the semantic deduction theorem by the exact equivalence between Gamma entailing A material-implies B and Gamma union A entailing B. The notation and source clauses, rather than the canon, remain the formal authority.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: derivation system; axiom; inference rule; derivable
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0063 titles the shared first-order/propositional wrapper and gives its reuse guidance. OLP-0064 defines a derivation as a finite syntactic object and an axiomatic derivation by fixed axioms or inference rules. OLP-0087 uses bisa diderivasi for the sentencehood consequence of the quantifier-elimination rules, preserving an explicit proof-theoretic relation instead of generic production. OLP-0088 gives the inductive and finite-tree definitions of a natural-deduction derivation and ties bisa diderivasi exactly to existence of such a tree from Gamma. OLP-0089 applies the same derivability vocabulary to each constructed disjunction branch and reaffirms that a lone assumption is itself a base-case derivation. OLP-0090 uses bisa diderivasi for quantified goals and contradictions and distinguishes formal derivation from generic production throughout the worked examples. Retain derivasi and the adapted proof-theory vocabulary under the borrowing policy; canon does not attest the complete compounds. OLP-0091 defines bisa diderivasi saka by a derivation whose conclusion is A and whose assumptions are discharged or belong to Gamma, then reuses that exact relation throughout the structural properties. OLP-0092 composes exact derivations of A and falsum, preserving their open assumption sets, negation inferences and resulting derivability claims. OLP-0093 preserves the exact conjunction, disjunction and conditional derivations, their premise order and every resulting formula. OLP-0094 preserves a named derivation of A(c) and the two one-step quantifier derivations with their exact premise and conclusion order. OLP-0095 analyzes eight exact proof trees and the remaining rule cases, preserving each premise derivation, conclusion and rule direction. OLP-0096 preserves identity introduction, both identity-elimination directions and four exact natural-deduction trees. OLP-0097 verifies the exact identity-elimination proof tree and keeps each premise derivation and conclusion in order. OLP-0099 states that every non-assumption signed formula results from an inference rule applied to an earlier formula on the same branch. OLP-0100 presents the eight connective inference rules and the optional Cut rule through exact signed-formula displays. OLP-0101 presents four signed quantifier inference rules, their side conditions and the substitution form of False existential. OLP-0102 defines every non-assumption tableau entry as the result of a correct inference-rule application to an entry above it on the same branch. OLP-0103 applies the signed connective inference rules step by step, preserving each source line, result line and rule label. OLP-0104 records every quantified and propositional inference rule beside its exact source line and resulting signed formula. OLP-0105 defines bisa diderivasi saka through a finite premise subset and a closed tableau for the false target together with the true premises. OLP-0106 uses Proves and bisa diderivasi through closed tableaux with exact finite signed premise sets, including both directions of the negation conversion. OLP-0107 uses bisa diderivasi for conjunction projections and pairing, disjunction injections, modus ponens and two conditional claims. OLP-0108 preserves a closed tableau for A(c), its converted universal witness and the two quantified instance derivability relations. OLP-0109 checks every nonsplitting and splitting tableau rule family, including the quantified cases and Cut, as a satisfiability-preserving expansion. OLP-0110 adds three exact identity inference rules to the tableau system and keeps both prerequisite formulas explicit for each signed replacement. OLP-0111 checks the reflexive and true identity rules explicitly and identifies the false-signed identity case as the exact dual. OLP-0112 assembles the complete axiomatic derivation chapter from its exact rule, proof, provability, soundness and identity imports. OLP-0113 defines the axiomatic derivation system, inference rules and derivability relation through the exact finite-sequence conditions. OLP-0114 defines the propositional axiom set and states modus ponens as the rule licensing A from earlier B and B implies A. OLP-0115 states the two quantified axioms and the two conditional inference rules while preserving each rule's exact direction and freshness condition. OLP-0116 follows each derivable target through its exact axiom instances and modus-ponens steps, including the Gamma-relative chain example. OLP-0117 uses the derivable predicate for each exact chained implication and then applies the quantified rule to the final universally quantified target. OLP-0118 fixes axiomatic derivability and theoremhood by the final formula of a derivation, then proves reflexivity, monotonicity and transitivity. OLP-0119 keeps premise sets and terminal formulas explicit in meta modus ponens and both directions of the deduction theorem.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: soundness; completeness; validity
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0064 fixes soundness as derivability guaranteeing entailment or validity and completeness as the converse. Retain the source term soundness with the descriptive gloss jaminan semantis so it cannot collapse into ordinary validity; OLP-0068 consequently renders a sound and complete system as one that ngemu jaminan semantis lan jangkep rather than reusing sah. OLP-0072 spells out the same soundness condition directly as the system deriving only valid sequents, again avoiding ordinary sah. Kelengkapan and validitas remain recognizable provisional adaptations because canon does not attest the metatheoretic terms. OLP-0091 states that soundness and completeness establish the mutual correspondence between the semantic and proof-theoretic notions, replacing a bare-sameness wording while preserving the theorem names. OLP-0095 states soundness as derivability from open assumptions implying semantic entailment and derives validity and consistency consequences. OLP-0105 states that soundness and completeness establish the mutual correspondence between semantic and tableau proof-theoretic notions, using cocog siji lan sijine rather than literal identity. OLP-0109 states tableau soundness as closed tableau implying unsatisfiability and derives validity, semantic consequence and consistency in that direction. OLP-0111 extends tableau soundness to identity by proving that no satisfiable closed tableau can result from any identity-rule expansion. OLP-0118 states that soundness and completeness together establish the correspondence between semantic and proof-theoretic notions.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: consistency; inconsistent; syntactic counterpart
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0064 defines inconsistency by arbitrary derivability and its semantic counterpart. OLP-0065 uses an empty-right sequent derivation, OLP-0066 derives falsity, and OLP-0067 uses a closed tableau from true-signed premises. The system-specific criteria and their arbitrary-derivability consequences remain source-controlled; canon does not attest the proof-theory compound. OLP-0091 defines ora konsisten exactly by derivability of falsum and defines consistency through the explicit outer negation of that property. OLP-0092 gives four exact relations between provability and consistency, including both complementary inconsistent extensions and explicit membership of not-A. OLP-0093 states the inconsistency of a disjunction with the negations of both disjuncts and realizes the claim by deriving falsum. OLP-0095 proves by contrapositive that satisfiability implies consistency, using derivability of falsum as the exact inconsistency criterion. OLP-0105 defines ora konsisten by a finite all-true premise set with a closed tableau and reuses that exact criterion in explosion and compactness. OLP-0106 applies ora konsisten to four exact tableau claims: contraction, the two provability equivalences, explicit inconsistency and exhaustive cases. OLP-0107 states that a disjunction with the negations of both disjuncts is ora konsisten and supplies the exact closed tableau witness. OLP-0109 proves by contrapositive that satisfiability implies consistency, using a finite closed-tableau witness for inconsistency. OLP-0118 defines axiomatic consistency through non-derivability of false and records the equivalent explosion characterization.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: sequent calculus; sequent; initial sequent; root
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0065 defines a sequent as two sentence sequences separated by the sequent symbol, with each side allowed to be empty, and defines a derivation as a tree from initial sequents to its root. OLP-0069 applies Kalkulus Sekuen as the exact shared FOL/PL chapter title and identifies the standard LK system without changing any tag or import. OLP-0070 gives the exact finite, possibly empty left/right sequence definition, names every tag-controlled initial-sequent variant, and places initial sequents at the top of derivation trees. The international proof-theory labels and ordinary tree-root word remain provisional because canon does not attest the complete technical senses. OLP-0099 uses oyod for the False-A root that defines a closed tableau for A and keeps the universal semantic conclusion explicit.
decisions.chosen_rendering: kalkulus sekuen; sekuen; sekuen wiwitan; oyod
decisions.rationale: OLP-0065 defines a sequent as two sentence sequences separated by the sequent symbol, with each side allowed to be empty, and defines a derivation as a tree from initial sequents to its root. The international proof-theory labels and ordinary tree-root word remain provisional because canon does not attest the complete technical senses. OLP-0099 uses oyod for the False-A root that defines a closed tableau for A and keeps the universal semantic conclusion explicit.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: natural deduction; introduction and elimination rules; proof by cases; indirect proof; conditional proof
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0066 ties proof by cases to both disjuncts, indirect proof to contradiction from the negated conclusion, and conditional proof to consequence from the antecedent, and each introduction or elimination label to its displayed rule. OLP-0085 defines the system's assumption start, paired introduction/elimination rules and sentence-tree derivations while describing its purpose as modeling informal mathematical reasoning. OLP-0086 verifies every propositional introduction and elimination direction, including disjunction case analysis and the distinction between negation introduction and classical falsehood. OLP-0088 defines the natural-deduction derivation structure inductively and illustrates conjunction and conditional introduction with exact discharge behavior. OLP-0089 gives stepwise bottom-up and top-down worked constructions using conjunction, disjunction, conditional and negation rules plus the classical falsehood rule. OLP-0090 extends that stepwise construction to quantified rules, including existential elimination, universal elimination, existential introduction and eigenvariable-aware negation proofs. Canon supports register, borrowing policy and an ordinary proof lexeme, not the complete proof-theory compounds. OLP-0091 fixes deduksi natural as the system in which theoremhood, derivability and the three structural properties are defined. OLP-0092 realizes the metatheoretic claims with five natural-deduction trees using negation introduction, negation elimination and classical falsehood. OLP-0093 realizes all propositional derivability claims with six natural-deduction trees using introduction and elimination rules. OLP-0094 uses natural-deduction universal introduction, existential introduction and universal elimination in the exact displayed directions. OLP-0095 verifies natural-deduction introduction and elimination cases by induction, including the classical falsehood and quantified rules. OLP-0096 combines identity with conditional and quantifier introduction and elimination in the displayed uniqueness derivation. OLP-0097 extends the natural-deduction soundness induction with the additional identity-elimination inference case.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: assumption; discharge; undischarged assumption
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0066 defines assumptions as leaf formulas, discharge as ending a temporary assumption's role at a numbered inference, and undischarged assumptions as the leaves that jointly support the conclusion. The final relation is stated as the conclusion being an akibat semantis from those assumptions rather than causal language. OLP-0085 fixes assumptions as topmost branch sentences, identifies the rules that discharge them and pairs each discharged assumption with the inference label. OLP-0086 makes discharge conditional and optional, with conditional introduction allowed to discharge any number of matching assumptions, including zero. OLP-0088 identifies the top sentences as Gamma assumptions or discharged assumptions, defines Gamma as the undischarged set, distinguishes the fully discharged theorem notation and displays a legal conditional-introduction step with no matching assumption to discharge. OLP-0089 tracks all numbered discharges through the worked trees and explicitly completes a rightmost conditional-introduction step that discharges no assumption. OLP-0090 tracks quantified-rule assumption dependencies and all nested discharge indices through three complete derivations. Canon does not attest the technical discharge vocabulary. OLP-0091 distinguishes fully discharged theorem derivations from derivations whose undischarged assumptions belong to Gamma, and its transitivity tree preserves the numbered discharge of A. OLP-0092 tracks every undischarged assumption location and all four numbered discharge operations through the displayed derivations. OLP-0093 explicitly lists the three undischarged assumptions in the disjunction proof and preserves both numbered discharge operations. OLP-0095 tracks every plural open-assumption set, both numbered discharges and every union of subderivation supports. OLP-0096 tracks three discharge-rule operations and both numbered assumption families through the nested identity derivation. OLP-0097 makes the two undischarged-assumption collections Gamma-one and Gamma-two explicitly plural before taking their union. OLP-0102 defines a tableau's initial assumption stem and distinguishes those assumptions from every later rule result. OLP-0103 begins each worked tableau from its exact signed assumptions and distinguishes them from every later rule result.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: tableau; signed formula; closed or open branch; truth tree
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0067 defines a signed formula as a truth-sign/sentence pair, a tableau as a downward-branching tree, closure by opposite signs on every branch, and model read-off from a saturated open branch. OLP-0064 supplies the truth-tree alias. The international method name and descriptive structural vocabulary remain provisional because canon does not attest the proof system. OLP-0099 defines a signed formula as one truth-value/sentence pair, sets tableau construction in a downward tree, defines closure by opposite signs on a branch and explains the false-root reading. OLP-0100 preserves every signed tableau expansion and distinguishes same-branch additions from split-branch alternatives. OLP-0101 uses a closed tableau as the exact counterexample showing why the two fresh-constant eigenvariable conditions are necessary. OLP-0102 gives the finite-tree tableau definition, exact open and closed branch criteria and a complete assumption-to-closure example. OLP-0103 constructs closed tableaux through exact opposite-sign branch witnesses and supplies three sets of closed-tableau exercises. OLP-0104 closes quantified tableau branches through exact opposite-sign instances and preserves 15 line-numbered trees. OLP-0105 uses tableau as the invariant project term in singular and generic contexts, and preserves every signed formula in theoremhood, derivability, consistency, transitivity and compactness witnesses. OLP-0106 transforms closed tableaux by true and false negation and combines two finite witnesses by Cut while preserving every signed formula and branch.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: axiom schema; modus ponens; inferential justification; resolution method; refutation
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0064 revalidates metodhe resolusi and refutasi as a mechanizable derivation alternative. OLP-0068 supplies the exact axiom-schema and modus-ponens roles and defines inferential justification by three exhaustive bases: axiomhood, premise membership or an inference rule. OLP-0090 reuses nduweni dhasar for the rule that warrants a final natural-deduction step, again keeping inferential support distinct from error correction. The international labels remain provisional adaptations rather than claimed canon attestation. OLP-0113 states modus ponens through its two earlier indexed formulas and keeps premise membership, axiomhood and rule licensing as three distinct bases. OLP-0114 preserves the complete labeled axiom family and the exact two-premise modus-ponens direction, then introduces MP as the rule abbreviation. OLP-0116 uses dhasar for inferential justification in the worked MP strategies and for the line justifications preserved by derivation concatenation. OLP-0117 combines the two instantiated consequences using the conjunction axiom and exactly two modus-ponens applications. OLP-0118 distinguishes an inferential basis from axiomhood and premise membership when the transitivity proof concatenates two derivations. OLP-0119 names modus ponens as the inferential basis of the final induction step, distinct from an axiom or membership in the premise set.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: eigenvariable; eigenvariable condition; closed term
decisions.intended_sense: Retain the international eigenvariable label and state its side condition and closed-term restriction transparently. OLP-0072 defines term katutup immediately as a term without variables, replaces the Indonesian-form tertutup, requires the eigenvariable constant to be absent from the lower sequent of right-universal or left-existential inference, and supplies the invalid derivation admitted when that condition is dropped. OLP-0076 applies the condition in a worked proof, orders the constrained left-existential step first, reuses the same term to reach an initial sequent and explicitly checks that the eigenvariable is absent from the lower end-sequent. OLP-0087 applies term katutup consistently to all four natural-deduction quantifier-rule explanations and preserves the distinct universal-introduction and existential-elimination freshness scopes. OLP-0090 applies eigenvariable-constrained rules early, reuses a consistently, checks every assumption dependency and states both final nonviolation checks with manawa content clauses. The exact proof-theory senses remain source-controlled and provisional. OLP-0094 states that c is absent from both Gamma and A(x), then uses those two freshness facts to satisfy the eigenvariable condition. OLP-0095 uses universal-introduction freshness in Gamma and A(x), an arbitrary assignment and the modified structure M-prime. OLP-0096 applies the established term katutup wording to every term restricted by the identity rules and substitutability example. OLP-0097 uses term katutup for the reflexive identity formula and states that its absence of variables makes assignments irrelevant. OLP-0101 consistently uses term katutup for True-universal and False-existential instantiation and states both branch-freshness conditions. OLP-0104 prioritizes the two fresh-constant rules, distinguishes them from repeatable closed-term instantiation and uses fresh a, b and c exactly where required. OLP-0108 states that c is absent from both Gamma and A(x), then uses those facts to justify the false-universal step below every premise formula. OLP-0109 uses a fresh constant in the false-universal case and a modified structure M-prime whose interpretation of that constant is fixed by a witness assignment. OLP-0110 applies the established term katutup to every term restricted by the identity-rule statement and the substitutability example. OLP-0111 fixes a variable assignment at the value of t-one, uses equality of term values and transfers satisfaction through extensionality to t-two. OLP-0115 uses term katutup for the substitution term shared by the universal-instantiation and existential-introduction axiom schemas. OLP-0117 applies QR only after deriving a conditional whose antecedent contains no occurrence of the generalizing constant a. OLP-0118's corrected monotonicity and transitivity proofs make the eigenvariable condition stable under enlarged premise contexts by uniformly renaming each clashing parameter to a fresh auxiliary constant in a temporary conservative language extension. OLP-0120 preserves the QR freshness condition in the quantified deduction-theorem induction. OLP-0123 and OLP-0125 use term katutup wherever quantified and identity axiom schemas require closed terms.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: proof-theoretic notion; provability; nonderivability; compactness
decisions.intended_sense: Retain the adapted theory/provability compounds, transparent negative phrase and established compactness formation. OLP-0077 defines the notions through finite LK derivations, relates proof-theoretic notions to their semantic counterparts, makes premise order and repetition immaterial through structural rules, defines consistency by absence of a finite empty-succedent derivation, and proves reflexivity, monotonicity, transitivity and both compactness clauses. OLP-0078 derives the main provability-consistency equivalences and inconsistency consequences with explicit finite witnesses and Cut. The canon supports register and borrowing only; these formal senses remain source-controlled and reversible. OLP-0091 revalidates gagasan teoretis-bukti, provabilitas, ora bisa diderivasi and kekompakan for natural deduction: the definitions and 79 mathematical spans control every specialist sense. OLP-0092 revalidates the derivability-consistency heading and the exact provability equivalences used later in the completeness proof. OLP-0093 revalidates the derivability-and-connectives heading and the exact projection, pairing, injection and conditional claims. OLP-0094 revalidates provability for strong generalization and the two quantified instance relations needed by completeness. OLP-0095 connects provability to entailment, premise-free validity and the consistency consequence fixed by the soundness theorem. OLP-0105 revalidates gagasan teoretis-bukti, provabilitas, ora bisa diderivasi and kekompakan for tableau metatheory: the definitions and 64 mathematical spans control every specialist sense. OLP-0106 revalidates the tableau derivability-and-consistency metatheory through four propositions and 71 source-controlled mathematical spans. OLP-0107 revalidates the derivability-and-connectives heading and the exact projection, pairing, injection and conditional tableau claims. OLP-0108 revalidates tableau provability for strong generalization and the existential-introduction and universal-instantiation directions. OLP-0109 connects tableau provability to validity, entailment and consistency through one preservation theorem and its three corollaries. OLP-0113 fixes axiomatic derivability by a derivation from Gamma whose final formula is A and fixes theoremhood by the corresponding empty-premise case. OLP-0116 proves transitivity of axiomatic derivability for chained conditionals by concatenating two Gamma-relative derivations and retargeting line references. OLP-0118 develops proof-theoretic notions through exact definitions, structural propositions and the finite-premise compactness argument.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: sound; soundness; satisfies a sequent; contrapositive
decisions.intended_sense: Retain the established sah-derived soundness term, ordinary satisfaction verb and adapted proof vocabulary. OLP-0081 defines sequent satisfaction through the antecedent-false or succedent-true alternatives, proves soundness by induction over every displayed inference family, and derives semantic consequence plus consistency from satisfiability. OLP-0083 extends the proof to identity's reflexive initial sequents and equality-replacement rules. The canon supports the language roles only; the formulas and proof cases control the specialist senses. OLP-0091 uses kontrapositif for the second compactness clause, with A identified exactly as falsum in the preserved formula. OLP-0095 revalidates Kasahihan, the guaranteed safety explanation and the final contrapositive proof for natural deduction. OLP-0097 proves soundness of natural deduction with identity by checking reflexivity and the equality-elimination induction case. OLP-0101 explains that the eigenvariable condition is needed for soundness by displaying the invalid formula that would otherwise close. OLP-0109 revalidates Kasahihan, the established sipat kaslametan explanation, signed-formula satisfaction and the final consistency contrapositive. OLP-0111 revalidates Kasahihan mawa identity as the closed-tableau nonsatisfiability claim proved by branch preservation.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: identity; substitutability of identicals; Leibniz's Law
decisions.intended_sense: Retain recognizable adapted labels and the descriptive substitutability phrase. OLP-0082 supplies both equality-replacement rules, the closed-term reflexive initial sequent, a substitutability example, and displayed symmetry and transitivity derivations; its explanation assigns A(x) in parallel on both sides. OLP-0083 verifies that the same closed-term and replacement machinery preserves validity. The canon supports register and borrowing only, so no Javanese proof-theory attestation is claimed. OLP-0096 revalidates identity introduction, replacement in both directions, substitutability of identicals, Leibniz's Law, symmetry and transitivity. OLP-0097 transfers satisfaction from A(t-one) to A(t-two) using semantic equality of term values and the cited extensionality result. OLP-0110 revalidates identity, substitutability of identicals and Leibniz's Law through the two signed replacement rules and three closed tableaux. OLP-0111 proves soundness for reflexive identity and signed substitutability using the same identity semantics as the preceding rule section.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: falsum; falsehood introduction; classical falsehood rule; intuitionistic logic
decisions.intended_sense: Use internationally recognizable adapted forms while the displayed rules control the exact inferential roles. OLP-0086 distinguishes inference from falsum to an arbitrary sentence from the classical rule that concludes A after deriving falsum under not-A. OLP-0089 explains why only falsehood introduction remains in intuitionistic logic, treats the classical rule as a last resort and uses it explicitly in the excluded-middle derivation and final exercise set. OLP-0090 applies the same classical rule qualification to all three final quantified exercises. OLP-0091 uses falsum as the exact conclusion defining inconsistency and as the special case in the compactness contrapositive. OLP-0092 derives falsum in each inconsistency direction and uses the classical falsehood rule exactly once to obtain A after discharging not-A. OLP-0093 derives falsum in the disjunction inconsistency proof and uses classical falsehood to obtain B in the not-A conditional proof. OLP-0095 uses falsum in negation introduction, classical falsehood and the impossibility argument establishing unsatisfiability.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: work from the bottom up; work from the top down; branch
decisions.intended_sense: Use ordinary directional and tree vocabulary rather than inventing a compact technical borrowing. OLP-0089 alternates between choosing a rule from the desired conclusion and extending assumptions downward, while its proof trees fix the relevant branch structure. OLP-0099 uses cabang for each root-to-application path, states when rules split or extend it and makes its joint-possibility reading explicit. OLP-0100 uses cabang for every tableau path and preserves which signed connective rules extend one branch and which split it in two. OLP-0102 preserves occurrence-sensitive rule application on a branch and extends every branch containing the selected occurrence. OLP-0103 distinguishes the top of a tableau from the end of each branch, requires expansion on both existing branches and preserves every split. OLP-0104 preserves every quantified branch split and the distinct instances used to close the left and right branches.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: satisfiable branch or tableau; prerequisite formula; result of a rule
decisions.intended_sense: Extend the established nyukupi and tableau vocabulary to branches and whole tableaux, and use ordinary prasyarat and asil for the inputs and output of an identity rule. OLP-0109 defines branch and tableau satisfiability, while OLP-0110's displayed identity rules fix the roles of both prerequisite formulas and their result. OLP-0109 directly defines a satisfiable branch and a satisfiable tableau, then preserves at least one such branch through every rule application. OLP-0110 identifies both prerequisite formulas for signed identity replacement and maps their line numbers in the symmetry and transitivity tableaux.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: axiomatic derivation; derivation sequence; axiom instance; hypothesis label; quantifier rule
decisions.intended_sense: Use the established derivation token with an adapted system label and ordinary words for sequence, instance and hypothesis; name the quantified rules descriptively. OLP-0113 defines derivations as finite formula sequences, OLP-0114 and OLP-0115 give the exact axiom and rule forms, and OLP-0116 explains the Hyp and MP labels. Canon supports academic register and general proof language but does not attest these formal senses. OLP-0113 revalidates the finite derivation sequence, axiom-instance and inference-rule vocabulary while preserving every index and terminal formula. OLP-0114 revalidates the propositional axiom and rule vocabulary against the complete 14-schema display and the MP inference clause. OLP-0115 revalidates the quantified axiom and rule vocabulary, both constant-freshness scopes and QR as the shared abbreviation for each rule. OLP-0116 revalidates the worked axiomatic derivations, the Hyp premise labels and the distinction between formula results and their premise set. OLP-0117 revalidates the quantified derivation vocabulary across both axiom instances, two chain applications, conjunction formation and QR generalization. OLP-0118 revalidates axiomatic metatheory vocabulary across derivability, theoremhood, consistency, structural properties, explosion and compactness. OLP-0119 reuses the finite derivation, axiom and Hyp-label vocabulary in the meta-MP derivation and both induction cases of the deduction theorem.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: formal meta-logic; formal methods; rigorous; rigor
decisions.intended_sense: Logika formal is directly attested, the official spelling guide supports adapted borrowing, and modern university prose supports metodhe and precise exposition. JV-P022 supplies historical mixed-script logic-teaching context only: its short Arabic excerpt is conditional, its interlinear gloss was not independently transcribed, and it supplies no particular modern loanword family. No source directly attests the two modern compounds, so they remain provisional. OLP-0044 renders completely rigorous as tliti babar pisan, keeping rigor distinct from beauty and geometric intuition. OLP-0046 uses luwih tliti and the ordinary derived noun katliten when questioning whether particular set encodings increase rigor. Neither passage adds the former unsupported phrase miturut paugeran matematis.

decisions.intended_sense: Reuse the established struktur, relasi nyukupi, formula, variable, element and function vocabulary, and use pangaji variabel as a reversible descriptive label for a function assigning domain elements to every variable. decisions.source_term_or_construction: substitution; universal instantiation; capture-sensitive replacement; term value; assignment update
decisions.intended_sense: Reuse the established formula, term, variable, derivation, satisfaction and assignment vocabulary, adapt substitution under the documented borrowing policy, and describe the substitution restriction through the danger of replacing bound occurrences or capturing variables. OLP-0146 fixes the senses through the P(a)-from-forall-v_0-P(v_0) example, the general A/x/t inference scheme, the warning that not every term is substitutable for every variable, and the equivalence between satisfaction after term substitution and satisfaction under an updated assignment. The canon supports formal register, orthography, controlled borrowing, ordinary relation language and a general proof lexeme only; the frozen formulas and later inductive definitions remain the formal authority.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: model and theory; model theory; axiomatic method; characterization by sentences; first-order expressibility
decisions.intended_sense: Reuse the established model, structure, sentence, semantic consequence, preorder, finite, infinite, enumerability, compactness and Löwenheim–Skolem vocabulary, and describe characterization and expressibility with ordinary scholarly Javanese. OLP-0147 fixes the senses through the definition of a model of Gamma, the model-theory and axiomatic-method directions, the exact two-sentence axiomatization of preorders, the iff between models and preorders, and the contrast among fixed finite size, infinitude, finitude and nonenumerability. The canon supports formal register, orthography, controlled borrowing, relation, equivalence and descriptive-method language only; the frozen definitions, formulas and metatheorems remain the formal authority.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: subformula; immediate subformula; proper subformula; recursive definition; transitive subformula relation
decisions.intended_sense: Reuse established formula, direct/immediate and proper-prefix diction. OLP-0155 fixes three distinct senses: immediate subformulas are only the arguments of the outermost formation step; proper subformulas are the transitive descendants excluding the formula itself; subformulas include the formula itself. The explicit-by-cases versus recursive distinction requires using only values at earlier smaller formulas. The source also controls transitivity and the exact 2n+1 upper bound. The canon supports formal register, orthography, controlled borrowing and ordinary relation and proof vocabulary, not native attestation for the complete technical hierarchy.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: first-order structure; n-place interpretation; standard arithmetic model; hereditarily finite sets; free logic; existential generalization
decisions.intended_sense: Reuse JV-T140, JV-T156 and the established n-panggonan language of the first-order-language section. OLP-0161 fixes a structure by nonempty domain, constant values, n-place predicate relations excluding identity, and n-place functions from domain^n to domain. It distinguishes the standard natural-number arithmetic model from arbitrary alternative structures, gives the iterative-power-set HF domain with actual membership, and explains how nonempty domains and denoting constants support existential validity and generalization, while free logic needs an extra existence premise. The consulted canon supports scholarly register, ordinary relation, function and truth language, orthography and controlled borrowing; the frozen source and formulas control every formal sense.

decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0170 presents five distinct examples. The strict-order axioms assert irreflexivity, total comparability and transitivity; group axioms specify right identity, associativity and a right inverse; Peano arithmetic includes successor, addition, multiplication, a definition of order and the induction schema. The pure-set example distinguishes empty set and urelements and derives unsatisfiability from naive comprehension using self-nonmembership. The mereological example treats parthood as a partial order and states a least-upper-bound-style sum condition; proper and improper parts remain distinct. Reuse JV-T028 for provisional comprehension and JV-T164 for order/model language. The consulted canon supports scholarly register, borrowing, ordinary member/relation/function wording and explanatory exposition; source formulas control the specialist senses.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: second-order logic; relation-variable quantification; comprehension schema; impredicative versus predicative comprehension; full versus weak semantics; categoricity and effective incompleteness; functions as relations; well-order, graph connectedness and many-sorted recoding
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0177 adds variables ranging over k-ary relations, uses comprehension with the relation variable not free in its defining formula, and distinguishes impredicative full comprehension from predicative restriction. Weak second-order structures select enough relations for comprehension; full structures contain every relation. The standard derivation system with comprehension is sound but no effective derivation system is complete for full semantics, whereas the minimal system is complete for weak semantics. Full semantics yields categorical arithmetic using induction over the range of the recursive map f, and expresses infinity, finiteness, well-ordering and graph connectedness. The last sections explain weak semantics through a many-sorted first-order encoding. Reuse JV-T028, JV-T122, JV-T170 and established derivation and satisfaction vocabulary. The consulted canon supports scholarly logic, truth, relation, function and member wording, orthography and controlled borrowing; source formulas and proof directions control every specialist claim.

decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0178 iterates set levels, treats types as syntactic labels, builds finite types by arrows and products, and gives typed term-formation rules for recursion, application, lambda abstraction, pairs and projections. Omega supplies truth values, the Church simple type theory is distinguished from the bare term system, and full function semantics is separated from weaker semantics admitting completeness. The intuitionistic and constructive claims are preserved as source claims. Reuse JV-T170 and JV-T171 for sort, relation, function, full/weak semantics and completeness. Consulted native Javanese passages support formal register, spelling, ordinary logic, truth, relation and function wording and controlled borrowing; source clauses and formulas control technical type theory.

decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0179 contrasts classical existence by cases with an explicitly given witness, using the Riemann-number anecdote and two irrational-exponent proofs. Its BHK account gives specific proof objects for conjunction, disjunction, implication, universal and existential quantification. The excluded-middle schemata, double-negation translation and classical-to-intuitionistic proof transfer must keep separate the pure-logical claim and the nonlogical-axiom caveat. The Kripke frame has a least world, monotone valuations and future-world implication forcing. Reuse existing proof, validity, derivation, semantics, relation and structure vocabulary, with source formulas controlling all technical senses. The consulted native canon supports scholarly logic register, truth wording, orthography, ordinary relation/function/member language and controlled borrowing; it does not directly attest these specialist intuitionistic terms.

Provability, epistemic and temporal readings are explicitly examples. S4 adds distribution, reflexivity and transitivity axioms plus necessitation; S5 adds possible-implies-necessarily-possible. The stated frame correspondences are reflexive/transitive for S4 and universal for S5. Reuse established formal logic and structure vocabulary, with source formulas and accessibility direction controlling technical senses. The consulted native canon supports formal scholarly register, ordinary logic/truth/relation wording, orthography and controlled borrowing; it does not independently attest modal model-theory terminology.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: Overspill section title; arbitrarily large finite models; finite satisfiability; compactness; first-order nondefinability of infinity
decisions.intended_sense: Despite the title Overspill, OLP-0186 proves by compactness that a theory with finite models above every size bound has an infinite model, then concludes that no single first-order sentence defines infinitude of the domain across structures. The proof adds countably many pairwise distinct constants and uses finite satisfiability of their inequalities. Preserve the source title as a technical borrowing without recasting the proof as a nonstandard-element overspill theorem. Consulted native canon supports formal register, ordinary logic, truth and member vocabulary, orthography and controlled borrowing; the quantifiers and compactness argument are controlled by the frozen source.

decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0187 distinguishes agreeing on all sentences from the stronger existence of a bijection preserving each named constant, predicate tuple and function value. Its term induction and assignment transfer show an isomorphism implies elementary equivalence, while an automorphism is a self-isomorphism. Ekuivalen elementer, isomorfisme and automorfisme are transparent provisional technical borrowings; ordinary Javanese scholarly equivalence and function passages support register, not a native specialist definition.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: theory of a structure; complete theory; informal theory; elementary equivalence; nonisomorphic enumerable model of real order
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0188 defines Theory(M) as all sentences true in M, notes its semantic closure, proves completeness by each sentence or its negation, and proves every model of Theory(M) elementarily equivalent to M. The informal use of theory need not be deductively closed. The real order in a one-predicate language is nonenumerable; an enumerable model of its consistent theory exists by Löwenheim–Skolem, so elementary equivalence does not reverse the preceding isomorphism theorem. Consulted Javanese canon supports scholarly register and ordinary truth, equivalence, relation and function wording, not direct native attestation of this complete model-theoretic sense.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: partial isomorphism; back-and-forth; quantifier rank; n-equivalence; finite language; atomic tuple relation; finite equivalence-class representatives
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0189 defines finite partial isomorphisms and a nonempty back-and-forth family; alternating extensions cover both enumerable domains and their union is an isomorphism. In purely relational languages, matching atomic tuples plus back-and-forth transfers formula satisfaction. Quantifier rank bounds the required recursion depth, and in finite signatures the converse uses finitely many equivalence classes of bounded-rank formulas. Isomorfisme parsial and ekuivalen-n are transparent technical borrowings; maju-mundur and tingkat kuantor describe the source mechanisms. Consulted canon supports scholarly enumeration, relation/function language, orthography and register, not specialist model-theory attestation.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: dense linear ordering without endpoints; Forth/Back extension proof; enumerable uniqueness; rational and real order elementary equivalence
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0190 lists irreflexivity, transitivity, trichotomy, no greatest element, no least element and density for one binary order predicate. The back-and-forth proof extends each finite order-preserving partial map and invokes the preceding enumerable-structure theorem. The final remark identifies every enumerable dense endpoint-free order with the rational order and uses the earlier enumerable model of the real order plus elementary-equivalence transitivity to derive R equivalent to Q; it also notes a direct partial-isomorphism route. Rapet describes density and tanpa titik ujung names both missing endpoints; the six formulas control the exact conditions. The Javanese canon supports scholarly register and ordinary relation/equivalence wording but not a specialist dense-order attestation.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: standard and nonstandard arithmetic models; standard numeral values; nonstandard element; consistency statement; derivation-code witness
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0192 contrasts the natural-number model with an isomorphic finite-a-string model and with compactness-produced nonstandard models containing elements outside the values of every standard numeral. The PA consistency example adds its negation consistently under the stated independence premise, so any resulting model is nonstandard and contains an element coding a supposed PA proof of contradiction even though no standard numeral can do so. Standar/nonstandar and model are controlled technical borrowings; the formulas fix the quantifier, negation and proof-predicate meanings. Consulted canon supports scholarly mathematical prose and ordinary truth/function wording, not direct native attestation of arithmetic model theory.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: nonstandard PA model; discrete strict order; predecessor; standard and nonstandard blocks; dense block order; countable reduct isomorphism
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0196 uses PA-provable conditions to make the model order strict, linear and discrete. Every nonzero element has one predecessor, while zero has none; a nonstandard element generates a two-sided successor block. Distinct blocks are disjoint and ordered uniformly, with no first nonstandard block, no last block in a nonstandard model, and a dense order among nonstandard blocks. Only for enumerable models is that dense endpoint-free quotient denumerable and isomorphic to the rational order; the conclusion concerns the reduct to order and equality, not full arithmetic isomorphism. The exact formulas, predecessor exception and block proofs determine technical meaning; consulted canon supports formal prose, orthography and ordinary relation/truth/function phrasing but not specialist native PA model-theory attestation.

decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0202 defines P explicitly by an L-formula C(x1,...,xn) and implicitly when Sigma(P) together with its uniform P-to-P-prime renaming forces agreement on P and P-prime. The frozen source and displayed formulas control these specialist distinctions. Consulted canon supports formal Javanese scholarly register, orthography, ordinary truth/relation language and controlled borrowing, not direct native attestation of Beth definability terminology.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: Lindström's Theorem; maximal logic; relational language; Downward Löwenheim–Skolem theorem
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0203 supplies the named chapter and ordered four-section wrapper. OLP-0204 describes first-order logic as maximal among logics meeting Compactness and Downward Löwenheim–Skolem under additional constraints, then restricts the chapter to relational languages with predicate symbols and individual constants but no function symbols. The named theorem references and source description govern the technical scope; existing JV-T132 and JV-T134 supply Teorema Kekompakan and the downward Löwenheim–Skolem wording. Consulted Javanese canon supports scholarly register, orthography, ordinary relation/function vocabulary and controlled borrowing, not native attestation of Lindström's abstract-logic result.

The frozen English clauses, preserved formulas and cross-reference fix these specialist meanings; existing JV-T176, JV-T179 and JV-T194 supply the reduct, isomorphism and Lindstrom context. Consulted native Javanese passages support scholarly exposition, enumeration, relation/equivalence vocabulary, orthography and controlled borrowing only, not native attestation of Lindstrom's abstract-logic terminology. The source's stated membership F in L(L) within the quantifier property is preserved verbatim in the displayed mathematics; no unverified source emendation is claimed.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: Compactness Property; Downward Löwenheim–Skolem Property; partial-isomorphism theorem for normal abstract logics; finite-sequence concatenation; enumerable model
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0206 extends the finite-subset compactness condition and enumerable-model condition to abstract logics, then states the partial-isomorphism-to-elementary-equivalence theorem under normality and the downward Löwenheim–Skolem property. The source proof introduces finite sequences, ternary concatenation/append relations, expanded structures and a back-and-forth relation. Existing JV-T132, JV-T134, JV-T181 and JV-T195 supply the compactness, enumerability, partial-isomorphism and abstract-logic terminology. The frozen formulas and cited definitions determine the specialist meanings; the consulted Javanese canon supports scholarly exposition, ordinary relation/function wording, enumeration, orthography and controlled borrowing only.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: primitive recursive function class; inductive closure; stage construction; zero, successor and projection base functions; dummy argument
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0213 first defines primitive recursion and composition by arity, then gives the smallest class containing unary Zero, Succ and all projections and closed under those two constructions. It presents stages S_i, derives addition through a three-place g obtained by composition, leaves multiplication as a stated proposition and exercise, and uses a dummy argument plus constants to fit h(y)=2^y into the k>=1 recursion schema. The frozen equations and arity constraints control these technical roles. JV-T200 through JV-T202 provide the previously established recursive and composition forms. Consulted Javanese canon supports academic exposition, enumeration, ordinary function vocabulary and borrowing policy, not specialist native attestation for the recursion-theoretic class.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: primitive recursive functions are computable; effective stepwise evaluation; closure of computability under primitive recursion and composition
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0215 demonstrates that if f and g are computable then each finite stage h(x,0), h(x,1), ... through h(x,y) can be computed, and notes that composition also preserves computability. Since Zero, Succ and projection functions are computable, every primitive recursive function is computable. The source asserts this one-way implication only; no converse is introduced. JV-T200, JV-T201 and JV-T203 establish the provisional recursive and computable forms. Consulted canon supports academic explanation and ordinary function language, not specialist native attestation for computability closure.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: primitive recursive relation; characteristic function; Boolean closure; bounded quantification; conditional case definition; less-than-or-equal correction
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0217 defines a primitive recursive relation by its 0/1 characteristic function, proves closure under negation, conjunction, disjunction and implication, then under bounded universal/existential quantification with vacuous y=0 cases and min/max recurrences. It uses a conditional function to build a prioritized piecewise function and leaves congruence modulo n as an exercise. JV-T200 and JV-T206 supply established provisional computability and truncated-subtraction terms. Consulted Javanese canon supports formal prose, relation/function vocabulary and orthography, not native attestation for these recursion-theoretic closure claims.

decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0219 shows x divides y through a bounded witness to x times z equals y, defines primality by nontrivial divisors, enumerates primes from p(0)=2, and bounds the next prime above x by x!+1 using Euclid's product argument. The recovered Javanese dictionary and government-edited arithmetic prose directly support ping-pingan, dipara, turah, and the coexistence of borrowed pembagian; earlier JV-T046 and OLP-0016 already used mbagi tanpa turah. They do not attest prima or this computability-theoretic construction, so wilangan prima and related specialized phrases remain reversible.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: computable but non-primitive-recursive function; effective enumeration; diagonal function; Ackermann–Péter growth; coding notations; Church–Turing thesis
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0223 uses an effective enumeration f_i of unary primitive recursive functions, defines computable evaluation g(x,y)=f_x(y), diagonal h(x)=g(x,x)+1, and concludes h and g are not primitive recursive. It then gives the Ackermann–Péter growth illustration and an explicit recursive coding of symbolic notations, while distinguishing an intuitive Church–Turing appeal from a later direct machine simulation. Earlier JV-T054 establishes diagonalisasi and JV-T204 the notation/enumeration vocabulary; OLP-0220 supplies finite-sequence codes. Consulted Javanese canon supports formal explanatory register, ordinary function phrasing, orthography and controlled borrowing, not specialist theorem attestation. All indices, constructors, growth equations, repeated-code caveat and proper names are controlled by the frozen source.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: Rice's theorem; index set; nontrivial extensional behavior; program syntax versus computed function
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0248 proves that a decidable index set defined by a class C of partial computable functions forces C to be empty or the whole class. Himpunan indeks refers to extensional saturation: indices computing the same function have the same membership. The text contrasts syntactic program questions with nontrivial questions about computed behavior. The proof chooses a nowhere-defined f outside C, a g in C, and an s-m-n index whose computed function equals f or g according to self-halting. Frozen English, formulas and proof control this technical meaning; consulted native passages support scholarly prose, spelling, controlled borrowing and ordinary function/semantic wording rather than specialist Rice-theorem attestation.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: fixed-point theorem; diagonal index transformer; self-reference; beta-equivalent Curry and Turing combinators
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0249 first contrasts an impossible computable halting decision with constructive program self-reference, then states equivalent fixed-point forms and proves the first by a primitive-recursive diag index transformer and a binary l whose own index is fed to diag. The source then gives five literal program/string examples and a lambda-calculus digression distinguishing common-reduct beta equivalence for Curry's Y from a stronger direct reduction for Turing's Y. Titik tetep and rujukan marang awake dhewe are transparent provisional descriptions; the exact formulas, code and English proof control technical meaning. The Javanese canon supports academic register, orthography, borrowing policy and ordinary explanatory/function phrasing, not specialist recursion or lambda-calculus attestation.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: self-referential function definition; greatest common divisor; fixed-point index versus ordinary recursion
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0251 obtains a partial computable f satisfying a self-referential branch equation from the fixed-point lemma, illustrates it with Euclidean gcd and a separate induction for totality, then distinguishes function recursion from the stronger index-based self-reference. Pambagi bebarengan paling gedhe is a transparent descriptive rendering of greatest common divisor; the source's recurrence and mod argument order fix the exact mathematics. Canon passages support academic register, digraph spelling, borrowing and ordinary function language, not native specialist recursion/gcd attestation.

decisions.source_term_or_construction: Turing-machine configuration; initial configuration; one-step yield; run; output; concatenation
decisions.intended_sense: OLP-0257 defines a configuration as a finite tape-symbol sequence, a head index below its length and a machine state. It defines initial configuration, one-step transition, runs, halting and a trimmed output string. Pangandhengan runtutan describes concatenation without implying arithmetic addition. Two further source-level edge conditions (empty input and overwritten marker) are recorded without speculative formula changes. Canon supports scholarly register, orthography and ordinary function/sequence wording, not specialist machine-semantics attestation.
